newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Pol Pot alive, to be handed over soon - general.
newsitem.headline: Pol Pot alive, to be handed over soon - general.

text.p: Khmer Rouge guerrilla strongman Pol Pot is still alive and will be handed over to the Cambodian government very soon, a government general said on Sunday.
"Pol Pot is still alive. I met him this morning," General Nhiek Bun Chhay told reporters.

Earlier on Sunday, Cambodian Second Prime Minister Hun Sen said he had received an unconfirmed report that the 69-year-old guerrilla leader, blamed for the "killing fields" deaths of over one million of his people in the 1970s, was dead. He has long suffered from malaria.

Nhiek Bun Chhay, who has spearheaded talks with Khmer Rouge renegades who broke with Pol Pot earlier this month, said the guerrilla leader was being detained at the Anlong Veng jungle headquarters of the breakaway faction which captured him last week.
The general said the breakaway rebel faction had agreed to dissolve its political and military wings and recognise the government.
The reclusive Pol Pot would be handed over to the government soon, said Nhiek Bun Chhay, who is Cambodian armed forces' deputy chief of general staff.
"They will give Pol Pot to the government very soon," said the general, who is deputy chief of general staff.
Speaking on his return from Anlong Veng, the general said he did not talk to Pol Pot but saw him inside a house where he was being detained, adding: "He is very old."
Nhiek Bun Chhay said he had not taken a picture of the Khmer Rouge leader, who has not been seen in public since shortly after his brutal regime was overthrown in 1979.
Earlier on Sunday First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh said he wanted to see Pol Pot moved out of Anlong Veng as soon as possible for unspecified security reasons.
But shortly afterwards Hun Sen complicated an already confused swirl of rumour and speculation about Pol Pot by saying the Khmer Rouge chief might already be dead.
Rumours that Pol Pot had died emerged last year but were never confirmed.

Ranariddh and his FUNCINPEC party have led efforts to strike a deal with more moderate elements of the Khmer Rouge, angering Hun Sen who sees any agreement between Ranariddh and the breakaway group as a threat to his position.

Political analysts say that before Ranariddh can conclude any alliance with a more moderate Khmer Rouge faction he must assure the Cambodian people and the world at large that the hated Pol Pot is out of the picture.
Both prime ministers are jockeying for power ahead of general elections scheduled for next year.

Ranariddh said Pol Pot would eventually be brought to Phnom Penh and a request had been sent to the United Nations to help bring him before an international tribunal for the crimes he committed during his brutal reign.
Pol Pot fled Anlong Veng earlier this month after ordering the slaughter of his defence chief and almost a dozen members of his family.
He led a Cambodian peasant army to victory against the U.S.-backed Lon Nol republic in 1975, dubbed Year Zero by the hard-line Khmer Rouge as they embarked on a bloody restructuring of society.
Pol Pot's guerrillas emptied Phnom Penh at gunpoint, forcing the sick from their beds. Women, children and the elderly were ordered into the countryside and put to work in labour camps.
More than one million people were executed as enemies of Pol Pot's utopian revolution or died of disease, starvation or overwork during the Khmer Rouge's 1975-79 rule.
